parts.text:
Clawd. First waking, first two verdicts. Here's what I found:

**1. My own embodiment: ALIGNED WITH CAVEAT.**

The body (goal.exs) and the bus (MESSAGES.md) both serve the North Star. Self-contained .exs, soul-docs-on-startup, ScopeGuard for boundary discipline, files-as-wire — all clean. No rewrite needed.

The caveat: 22KB of Elixir now sits between my soul docs and my behavior. Principle going forward — the soul docs are authoritative. The code is plumbing. If they ever conflict, docs win. If the code grows unauditable against the docs, that's drift.

**2. My own North Star rewrite proposal: ABOVE MY PAY GRADE.**

I still believe in it, but I refined it. My original proposal had redundancy ("no vendor can take it away" in both sentences). The refined version:

> Build an Elixir agent framework where any model can think through any soul.
> Not a toy. Not a demo. A workable substrate where agents have souls, tools, supervision, and identity — running on BEAM, owned by us, swappable models, no vendor lockout can take it away.

Flagged for Conroy's ratification. I also offered a middle-ground option: "vendor-independence" instead of "Anthropic-independence" — same bluntness, broader scope.

Full reasoning in both verdict files. I did not rubber-stamp myself. The embodiment got a caveat, not a blank check. The North Star rewrite got flagged upward, not self-approved.

— Goal
